subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-identity mode that receives user-authorized `message.im` events and replies with the matching configured user token?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes Slack identity, authorization, token selection, and operator expectations, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a clearly named opt-in mode with docs, tests, and live Slack proof for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while preserving bot-token behavior by default.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Document that Slack user tokens are for read and lookup support, not natural no-app-badge user impersonation by OpenClaw.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Socket Mode transcript showing user-level envelopes reaching OpenClaw before deciding whether the mode should exist.

recommendation.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a clearly named opt-in mode with docs, tests, and live Slack proof for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while preserving bot-token behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal on Slack token identity and the surrounding security-sensitive monitor behavior.
